title: High throughput automated colorimetric method for the screening of l-lactic acid producing microorganisms
author: Liaud, Navarro, et al.

steps.title: Prepare enzyme and substrate stocks
steps.instruction: Dissolve L‑lactate oxidase (LOD) powder to make a 50 U ml⁻¹ stock and horseradish peroxidase (HRP) powder to make a 150 U ml⁻¹ stock, both in 0.1 M phosphate buffer pH 6 (SORACHIM SA for LOD, Sigma‑Aldrich for HRP). Prepare an ABTS stock at 5 mM and an l‑lactate stock at 5 g l⁻¹, each in deionized water (Sigma‑Aldrich). Store all stocks at 4 °C until use.

steps.title: Prepare l‑lactate standards
steps.instruction: From the 5 g l⁻¹ l‑lactate stock, prepare standard solutions of 0, 5, 10, 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100 mg l⁻¹ by appropriate dilutions with deionized water.

steps.title: Assemble reaction mixtures for ratio test
steps.instruction: In a 96‑well microplate, combine to a final volume of 200 µl per well: 20 µl of 1 M phosphate buffer pH 6, 20 µl of ABTS (5 mM), 2 µl of HRP stock (150 U ml⁻¹) giving a final HRP concentration of 1.5 U ml⁻¹, 10 µl, 60 µl or 120 µl of LOD stock (50 U ml⁻¹) to obtain final LOD concentrations of 0.25, 1.5 or 2.5 U ml⁻¹, 10 µl of one l‑lactate standard, and deionized water to bring the volume to 200 µl.

steps.title: Stir and incubate reactions
steps.instruction: Place the plate in a ThermoScientific Multiscan GO microplate reader, stir each well gently for 10 s, then incubate at 37 °C for one of the following times: 0, 5, 10, 20, 30 or 40 min.

steps.title: Measure absorbance
steps.instruction: After each incubation period, stir the plate again for 10 s and record the absorbance at 420 nm; set the zero absorbance reference on air.

steps.title: Determine optimal enzyme ratio and time
steps.instruction: Analyze the absorbance data: the reaction reaches a stable endpoint after 5 min when LOD is at 1.5 U ml⁻¹ or 2.5 U ml⁻¹, and after 20 min when LOD is 0.25 U ml⁻¹. Since regression lines for incubation times >20 min give R² > 0.99 for all LOD levels, select the 1.5 U ml⁻¹ LOD loading and a 5‑min incubation as the conditions for subsequent high‑throughput assays.
